analysis.title: Princeton alumni remove microplastics from Atlantic City wastewater

claims.text: The Atlantic City wastewater treatment facility said the new initiative aims to divert microplastics from the ocean, protecting marine life and humans.
However, the Atlantic County Utilities Authority said it’s crucial to remove the contaminants from wastewater before being discharged into the environment.
Liu, PolyGone’s co-founder and chief operating officer, said the technology also stands out for its sleek design, which she credits to their background as architecture students.

The technology designed by PolyGone Systems, a startup founded by Nathanial Banks and Yidian Liu, replicates ultrahydrophobic plants found in wetlands that microplastics easily stick to so the contaminant can be removed from water.
PolyGone’s founders say the technology has been able to remove more than 98% of microplastics in the control lab environment.
Liu and Banks have launched a similar system for a wastewater treatment plant in California, and say they’re also interested in scaling down their technology for residential uses.
These particles have been detected in the human bloodstream, brain tissue and other organs, and some researchers say exposure could increase the risk of heart attack or stroke.
The utility said the installation, which is fully funded by a federal grant, is the first of its kind in the world.
